title: Colosseum
blurb: The Flavian Amphitheatre in Rome, modeled in its complete original form as dedicated in AD 80, including Domitian's hypogeum and the wooden top gallery. Explore 128 components across 9 systems, from the 80 travertine arches to the 240 velarium mast corbels.

systems.name: Outer Facade
systems.description: Travertine arcade tiers: Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian bays around the full ellipse.

systems.name: Attic and Velarium
systems.description: Upper attic story, crowning cornice, and the retractable velarium awning.

systems.name: Main Entrances
systems.description: Four unnumbered axial entrances and 76 numbered spectator entrances.

systems.name: Seating Cavea
systems.description: Tiered marble seating for about 50,000 spectators, strictly ordered by class.

systems.name: Circulation
systems.description: Annular corridors, vomitoria, and stairs that moved the crowd.

systems.name: Support Structure
systems.description: Radial and annular walls carrying the cavea.

systems.name: Arena
systems.description: Wooden sand covered floor and its surrounding wall.

systems.name: Hypogeum
systems.description: Domitian's subterranean tunnels, cages, and lifting machinery.

systems.name: Materials
systems.description: Representative samples of the building's key materials.

explanations.velarium canopy: The velarium was a canvas covered, net like structure made of ropes with a hole in the center. It covered two thirds of the arena and sloped down toward the center to catch the wind and give the audience a breeze. The fabric shape is schematic.
explanations.stylobate base ring: The outer wall stands on a raised two step travertine stylobate.
explanations.travertine pavement and cippi: A 17.50 m wide travertine pavement surrounds the building; five stone cippi posts still stand on the east side, 18 m out from the perimeter.
explanations.north axial entrance portal: The northern axial entrance was reserved for the Roman Emperor and his aides. Its arches were wider and more highly ornamented than the rest, and a wide passage led from it directly to the imperial box (pulvinar) on the podium.
explanations.north entrance arch: The decorated arch framing the northern imperial entrance. All four axial entrances were richly decorated with painted stucco reliefs, of which fragments survive.
explanations.south axial entrance portal: The southern axial entrance, at the south end of the minor axis, served the imperial family. Like the northern entrance, its arches were wider and more highly ornamented than the rest.
explanations.south entrance arch: The decorated arch framing the southern imperial entrance, richly decorated with painted stucco reliefs like the other three axial entrances.
explanations.east axial entrance: The major axis entrances led directly into the arena, admitting processions and equipment.
explanations.west axial entrance: The western major axis entrance led directly into the arena.
explanations.numbered spectator entrances (76): 76 of the 80 ground arches were numbered entrances for ordinary spectators; entrances XXIII to LIIII still survive on the north side.
explanations.porta triumphalis (east arena gate): The Porta Triumphalis, the eastern gate of the arena at the end of the major axis, through which gladiators and wild animals entered and by which victorious combatants departed.
explanations.porta libitinensis (west arena gate): The Porta Libitinensis, the western gate of the arena, through which the mortally wounded and the dead were carried out.
explanations.podium ring: Senators sat on a marble podium raised about 4 m above the arena, fronted by a bronze balustrade.
explanations.ne maenianum primum wedges: NE wedges of the maenianum primum: about 20 rows of marble covered seats reserved for the knightly class (equites). The seating was divided into wedge shaped sections (cunei) by steps and aisles, and each seat could be designated by its row, wedge, and number. The four way split is schematic.

explanations.imperial box (pulvinar): The pulvinar, the imperial box, on the podium at the north end of the minor axis, reached by a wide passage from the northern entrance.
explanations.imperial box canopy: The canopy sheltering the imperial box (pulvinar). Its form is schematic.
explanations.box of the praefectus urbi: The prefect of the city had his own box on the podium, opposite the imperial box.
explanations.roof standing room: About 5,000 of the poorest spectators, the pullati, stood on the flat roof behind a 5 m colonnaded wall.
explanations.praecinctiones and baltei: Horizontal walkways (praecinctiones) and low parapet walls (baltei) divided the seating tiers by social class.
explanations.ground floor outer ambulatory: The outer of two lofty arched corridors encircling the building at ground level between the outer wall and the third wall.
explanations.ground floor inner ambulatory: The inner of the two ground floor annular corridors serving the seating.
explanations.second floor outer corridor: The outer annular corridor of the second story, distributing spectators to the middle seating tiers.
explanations.second floor inner corridor: The inner corridor of the second story, divided into an upper and a lower section, with ingeniously arranged flights of steps leading to the topmost story.
explanations.third floor outer corridor: The outer annular corridor of the third story, serving the upper seats and the wooden gallery.
explanations.third floor inner corridor: The inner corridor of the third story, with ingeniously arranged flights of steps leading to the topmost story and the upper part of the second tier of seats.
explanations.grand staircase, north: A monumental stair near the northern axial entrance, connecting the ground floor ambulatory with the upper corridors. Its exact form and routing are schematic.
explanations.grand staircase, south: A monumental stair near the southern axial entrance, connecting the ground floor ambulatory with the upper corridors. Its exact form and routing are schematic.
explanations.vomitoria passages: Stair passages were arranged in fours and could disgorge the crowd in only a few minutes; the name vomitoria comes from this spewing forth.
explanations.radial stair flights: Radial stair flights climbed the cavea slope between the wedge shaped seating sections.
explanations.ne radial support walls (20): NE radial support walls: twenty of the eighty radiating walls that matched the lower arcade piers in number and carried the sloping cavea floor with its marble seats.

explanations.inner annular support wall: The inner of the concentric annular walls tying the radial walls together beneath the seating slope. Its exact radius is schematic.
explanations.outer annular support wall: The outer of the concentric annular walls tying the radial walls together beneath the seating slope. Its exact radius is schematic.
explanations.second inner wall: The second inner wall stands 5.80 m inside the outer wall.
explanations.third inner wall: The third inner wall stands 4.50 m inside the second.
explanations.east travertine pressure skeleton: East half of Vespasian's inner travertine skeleton, which carried the greatest structural loads and rose no higher than the second story. Column positions are schematic.
explanations.west travertine pressure skeleton: West half of Vespasian's inner travertine skeleton, which carried the greatest structural loads and rose no higher than the second story. Column positions are schematic.

explanations.arena sand surface: The sand (harena, the origin of the word arena) strewn over the wooden arena floor. The surface is schematic.
explanations.arena wall: A 5 m high wall ringed the arena, above which the seating rose.
explanations.arena fence: A fence built to protect the spectators from the attacks of the wild beasts, running all round the arena.
explanations.marble passage behind the fence: A narrow marble paved passage behind the arena fence, below the senators' podium.
explanations.hypogeum central corridor: The central gallery of the hypogeum, running along the major axis between substructure walls 5.50 to 6.08 m high standing on a brick pavement.
explanations.north hypogeum chambers: North side chambers of the hypogeum, where gladiators and animals were held before contests. The internal room layout is a simplified schematic grid.
explanations.south hypogeum chambers: South side chambers of the hypogeum, where gladiators and animals were held before contests. The internal room layout is a simplified schematic grid.
explanations.north animal dens: North dens for wild beasts in the hypogeum substructures. Their exact positions are schematic.
explanations.south animal dens: South dens for wild beasts in the hypogeum substructures. Their exact positions are schematic.
explanations.east gladiator passage: East gladiator passage: the hypogeum held gladiators before contests, and tunnels linked it to the outside, including the gladiators' barracks at the Ludus Magnus to the east. Passage routing is schematic.
explanations.west gladiator passage: West gladiator passage: the hypogeum held gladiators before contests, and tunnels linked it to points outside the building. Passage routing is schematic.
explanations.lower tunnel corridors: The lower level corridors of Domitian's two level subterranean tunnel network.
explanations.tunnel connecting ramps: Ramps connecting the two levels of the hypogeum tunnel network. Their exact routing is schematic.
explanations.ne vertical shafts (20): NE vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.
explanations.nw vertical shafts (20): NW vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.
explanations.se vertical shafts (20): SE vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.
explanations.sw vertical shafts (20): SW vertical shafts: twenty of the eighty shafts that gave caged animals and scenery instant access to the arena floor.
explanations.elevator winch drums: Slave powered winch drums that worked the elevators and trapdoors of the hypogeum.
explanations.pulley rigging posts: Elevators and pulleys that raised and lowered scenery, props, and caged animals to the surface for release.
explanations.east hegmata platforms: East hinged hegmata platforms, which tilted up through trapdoors to deliver animals, scenery, and even elephants to the arena.
explanations.west hegmata platforms: West hinged hegmata platforms, which tilted up through trapdoors to deliver animals, scenery, and even elephants to the arena.
explanations.major axis subterranean passage: A subterranean passage on the line of the major axis, by which the hypogeum substructures were entered.
explanations.minor axis subterranean passage: A subterranean passage on the line of the minor axis, by which the hypogeum substructures were entered.
explanations.cryptoporticus of commodus: The cryptoporticus of Commodus was a vaulted underground passage linking the imperial areas to the arena.
explanations.travertine block sample: The outer wall used over 100,000 cubic meters of travertine set without mortar, held by 300 tons of iron clamps. Representative sample shown.
explanations.brick faced concrete sample: Inner walls are concrete with and without brick facing. Representative sample shown.
explanations.tuff and sperone sample: Tuff and sperone, volcanic stones, were used in the lower parts of the inner walls. Representative sample shown.
explanations.marble seat sample: Marble faced the seats of the cavea and the podium. Representative sample shown.
